thread:
jessica: seeing RDMA heartbeat failures between gpu-pool pods in us-west-2a, started ~10:10UTC. Some pods lose KV sync and drop replicas.
 samir: any recent netpol changes in gpu namespaces?
 jessica: we rolled a 'restrict-egress' netpol to gpu-ns to lock down external egress last night. thought it only targeted 0.0.0.0/0.
 ryan: can you paste the netpol?
 jessica: ```yaml
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: restrict-egress
  namespace: gpu-ns
spec:
  podSelector: {}
  policyTypes:
  - Egress
  egress:
  - to:
    - ipBlock:
        cidr: 10.0.0.0/8
    ports:
    - protocol: TCP
      port: 80
```
 lucy: ahh that ipBlock only allows 10.0.0.0/8 — our svcCIDR is 10.96.0.0/12 but we use ClusterIP translation across nodes and the RDMA flows are using host-networked paths with ephemeral ports.
 samir: but RDMA heartbeat is on UDP/20000-ish? it's not TCP/80.
 jessica: right. the netpol rule is too narrow and only allowed TCP:80 to 10.0.0.0/8. everything else egress is blocked.
 devops-oncall: infra-bot reports: `netpol/applied: gpu-ns/restrict-egress by lucy at 2024-05-01T03:02Z`
 ryan: quick check: can a pod curl the cluster IP of kv-store?
 jessica: `kubectl exec -n gpu-ns gpu-pod-1 -- curl -sS http://10.96.0.12:9200` -> timeout
 lucy: show `kubectl get pods -n kube-system -o wide` and `iptables -t nat -L -n` on host?
 jessica: attaching snippet: ```
# on node
iptables -t nat -S | grep KUBE-SERVICES
-A KUBE-SERVICES -d 10.96.0.12/32 -p tcp -m comment --comment "default/kv svc" -j KUBE-MARK-MASQ
```
 samir: so ClusterIP translation exists but netpol operates at L3/L4 before host NAT for egress. our netpol prevented pod from reaching the host IP/port used for cross-node RDMA tunneling.
 ryan: does the cluster use CNI egress policy in addition to k8s netpol (we use calico)? calico has global egress policies that might interact.
 lucy: calico is in use; but this was a k8s NetworkPolicy with podSelector:{} (applies to all pods in namespace). calico enforces it.
 jessica: suggestion: add an egress rule permitting cluster service CIDRs and the RDMA port ranges and UDP. e.g. `- to: - ipBlock: cidr: 10.96.0.0/12` and allow UDP 20000-20010 plus TCP 9300-9400 etc.
 devops-oncall: rolling a patch to allow svcCIDR and RDMA port range now. will canary to 1 node first.
 infra-bot: deploy job started: `patch networkpolicy/restrict-egress gpu-ns` by devops-oncall
 samir: also consider using namespaceSelector for kube-system or a serviceAccount exception so control-plane traffic keeps working if we later tighten rules.
 ryan: after patch, monitor `cilium monitor` / `calicoctl get felixconfig` for drops.
 jessica: patched at 10:24UTC, canary on node us-west-2a-ig1. checking KV replicas...
 jessica: KV sync recovered on canary pods. RDMA heartbeats resumed. CPU on replica leader dropped back to normal.
 lucy: follow-up: update the network policy doc template to include a checklist: include svcCIDR ranges, host-network ports used by infra, and a verification step: `kubectl exec` to reach cluster IPs + run inter-pod `iperf` on RDMA port.
 ryan: logging an infra PR to add that checklist + example netpol snippets.
 jessica: thanks all. leaving this thread open for 24h to watch for regressions.
 infra-bot: incident-note created: "netpol-too-restrictive-blocked-clusterip-rdma"
 devops-oncall: thumbs up :thumbsup:
